subject: ventures/course-launch-revenue-calculator
professional: a course-business launch strategist / finance consultant who builds launch P&Ls for creators (funnel math, payment plans, affiliate/JV launches, ad CPA)

evidence.correctness: Ran the engine via node and recomputed three cases in python3 from the funnel definitions (not from the author's tests). Sample job (list 4000, 12% visit, 2.5% buy, $1500 ads at $1.20 CPC, 1.2% paid conv, $297, 6% refunds, 2.9%+$0.30, 5% platform, 20% affiliate share at 30%, $800 fixed): buyers 480*0.025+1250*0.012=27; net/buyer 297-17.82-9.213-13.959-16.7508=239.5572; net 27*239.5572-2300=4168.0444; ROAS 15*239.5572/1500=2.3956; break-even buyers 2300/239.5572=9.6010, blended rate 9.601/1730=0.5550% -- engine identical to 4 dp. Second case ($497, 10% refunds, 5000 list, 15%/3%, $5000 fixed): net 4733.2075, break-even list 2568.53 -- identical; price-ladder buyersToMatch at 1x = 22.5 = buyers. Third case (net vs gross ROAS) 0.9695 as defined. The 2.9%+$0.30 default and 'processor fee kept on a refund' match Stripe's published standard US online rate and refund policy (as cited by ventures/card-processing-fee-audit/calc.mjs:37 and merchant-of-record-fee-calculator/engine.mjs:23 to stripe.com/pricing; stripe.com was unreachable from this session, so not re-read live). Arithmetic is right; held at 3 because 'Return on ad spend' is computed on net contribution, not the revenue/spend definition a marketer reads ROAS as.
evidence.completeness: README/page features checked end to end via the engine: net profit, where-the-money-goes lines (sum to net), break-even buyers/visit-to-sale rate/list size, ROAS, warnings (fees eat price, ROAS<1, paid>list conversion, >10% conversion), conversion scenarios 25-150%, price table with buyers-to-match, CSV export (reportCsv run), local usage counters with opt-out. All five related-tool links resolve to existing ventures. served-copy.mjs: no placeholder or retired origin left. No TODOs or stubs. Computed-but-unshown profitPerListMember is the only loose end.
evidence.verification: node --test '*.test.mjs' in the venture: 29 pass, 0 fail (calc, page, usage). 4 seeded mutants with quality_mutate.py: processor fee scaled by kept share CAUGHT; >10% conversion warning threshold moved to 15 CAUGHT; break-even list ignoring paid buyers SURVIVED (no test combines ads with a list and fixed costs); ROAS on gross instead of net SURVIVED (the only ROAS test uses zero fees so net==gross). Half the headline-output mutants survive.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (156 lines), index.html inline script, usage.mjs, all three test files. Pure functions, NaN/negative/over-100 inputs rejected, comma and $ stripped ('1,200' parses), esc() on all injected text, no network calls (page test enforces). Defects: error messages expose internal keys ('Check the number in "convPct"'); profitPerListMember computed and never shown (dead output); a list with 0% visit passes validation and reports '0 copies, roughly breaks even'; missing comma in footer related-tools sentence.
evidence.claims: Checked: 'nothing is uploaded' (no fetch/XHR, page test enforces) backed; formulas in 'How it is calculated' match calc.mjs lines 36-97; FAQ 1,000 x 10% x 2% = 2 sales correct; 'Not modelled' list (tax, payment plans, upsells, price elasticity) is explicit; 'Unverified against a real launch's books' stated; disclaimer and 'not affiliated' present in footer and README; no platform named or ranked, so no unbacked Teachable/Kajabi/Thinkific rates. Weakness: the 'Return on ad spend' tile uses net-after-fees contribution, which the FAQ and method define, but the label alone reads as standard ROAS. Default 2.9%+$0.30 is uncited on the page (it is presented as an editable default, not a claim).
evidence.fitness: Walked a creator's job: pre-launch 'is my list big enough and do ads pay?' -- answerable in under a minute with sensible outputs and break-even list size. A launch strategist's first-hour gaps: no payment plan option (most $297-$997 launches offer one, with default rates), affiliate share only adds cost and never adds buyers so a JV/affiliate launch cannot be modelled, single price tier (no VIP tier or order bump), no save/share link to compare scenarios.
evidence.domain: Compared with standard launch P&L practice (list x open/click/visit x conversion; CPA vs net per buyer; refund-window clawback of affiliate commissions; non-refunded Stripe fees). Matches on refunds, processor fees and commission clawback. Departs on: ROAS defined on net contribution rather than revenue/spend (practitioners compare gross ROAS with a break-even ROAS); affiliate sales modelled as a share of your own buyers rather than an additional traffic channel; payment plans and their default rate omitted; platform fee assumed refunded on refunds, not checked against any platform's terms (page tells user to check).

defects.what: 'Return on ad spend' tile is net-after-fees contribution per ad dollar, not revenue/ad spend; a marketer comparing it with Meta/Google ROAS or a break-even ROAS reads it wrong (0.97x shown where gross ROAS is 1.00x)
Break-even list size subtracting paid buyers is untested: seeded mutant that drops the subtraction survives
ROAS net-vs-gross is untested: the only ROAS test has zero fees, so a gross-ROAS mutant survives
Affiliate sales are a share of your own buyers that only add commission cost; affiliates never add buyers, so a JV/affiliate launch cannot be modelled
No payment-plan option (instalment count, take rate, default rate), a standard part of a priced course launch; stated as not modelled
Validation errors show internal field keys ('convPct', 'listSize') instead of the field labels
A list with 0% visit rate (or 0% conversion) and no ads passes validation and reports '0 copies, roughly breaks even'
profitPerListMember is computed but never shown or exported
Default 2.9% + $0.30 processor fee has no source or date on the page
Missing comma in related-tools sentence ('Patreon fee calculator the freelance...')

verdict: A small, honest launch P&L calculator whose arithmetic is right: three cases recomputed independently in python matched the engine to four decimals, the refund treatment matches Stripe's published policy, and every page claim is backed with a clear not-modelled list and disclaimer. It misses the bar on verification (2 of 4 seeded mutants in headline outputs survive: break-even list size with ads, and net-vs-gross ROAS) and is held below a launch strategist's sign-off on domain and fitness: its ROAS is net contribution under a standard label, affiliates cannot add buyers, and payment plans are absent. Finished (completeness 3), not at the bar.
